row.evidence: Okta's YardiOne listing says it 'allows users to authenticate securely through single sign-on (SSO) with SAML along with provisioning of users and groups via SCIM', but no first-party Yardi page states which plan includes it or its price.
row.notes: Status changed from partial to unknown. SCIM exists for YardiOne with catalogue apps in both Okta (Create, Update, Deactivate, Group Push) and Entra, so the June 'partial' no longer fits the rules (two IdPs, full lifecycle). June's gate ('Voyager Enterprise via YardiOne, $30K-$150K+/yr') had no loadable first-party source and is dropped: yardi.com returns 403 to curl, WebFetch and the headless renderer. Breeze pricing is per unit ($1/unit/mo, $100 minimum residential; Premier $400 minimum), not per user, and Breeze pages never mention SSO, SCIM or YardiOne. Provisioning is enabled through YardiOne support. YardiOne also supports SAML JIT.

plans.notes: YardiOne is the sign-in platform across Yardi applications; SAML SSO and SCIM are documented on the Okta and Entra catalogue pages. Which Yardi subscriptions include YardiOne, and at what price, could not be confirmed: yardi.com returns 403 to every fetch method.

auth.token_source: Tenant URL and Secret Token from YardiOne support

limitations.text: Provisioning is switched on by YardiOne support, not self-service.

scim.notes: Product is YardiOne. Provisioning must be enabled by YardiOne support, which supplies the tenant URL and secret token. All SCIM detail comes from IdP catalogue pages; Yardi publishes no SCIM documentation that could be loaded.

okta.notes: OIN 'YardiOne' ticks SAML, SCIM, Create, Update, Deactivate, Group Push. A separate older OIN 'Yardi' app is SWA only.

fallbacks.notes: docs_public false: no first-party SCIM or API documentation could be loaded (yardi.com 403).
